plant.cvs: 'Fire Power' – dwarf, red winter foliage · OBSESSED ('Seika') – upright, red new growth · 'Gulf Stream' – compact, bronze-red tints · 'Richmond' – taller, heavy berrying
plant.foliage: evergreen; finely divided pinnate leaves, red when young and in cold weather
plant.hardinessNote: Hardy through most of the UK in an average winter, approximately -10 to -5°C; this is the species band, not checked for this cultivar.
plant.pollination: not applicable; sold for its foliage
plant.prune: Little needed. Remove dead or damaged stems in spring, and cut a few of the oldest stems to the base to keep it bushy.
plant.resilience: Generally tough and trouble-free once established. Foliage can scorch in cold, drying winds. Pests: few significant pests in the UK.

plant.toxicity: Toxic if eaten: all parts, especially the berries, contain cyanogenic compounds. Keep children, dogs and cats from chewing it.
uncertain: hardiness: H4 is the RHS band for Nandina domestica as remembered. I could not confirm a separate rating for 'Red Light'.
height and spread: no confident figures for this cultivar. It is believed to be compact, roughly 1 m, but this was not stated, to avoid guessing.
peak: unsure whether it is sold mainly on spring new growth or on autumn-winter colour, so this was left blank.
hue: based on the red foliage the name suggests and my recall. Exact shade not verified.
compliance: unknown whether 'Red Light' carries plant breeders' rights or a trade name, so no number was given.
clay: Nandina is often said to tolerate heavier soils that do not waterlog, but this is not established for this cultivar.
pollination: unsure whether 'Red Light' flowers or berries reliably, so it was treated as a foliage plant.
sunMin and sunNeed: judged from the species, which colours best in sun and tolerates part shade.

ratings (pestRisk, thirst, careLevel, growthSpeed): judged from general knowledge of compact Nandina cultivars.
toxicity: the cyanogenic glycosides in Nandina, and the risk to pets and birds from the berries, are species-level knowledge applied to this cultivar.
plant.uses: Borders · containers · low hedging · patio planting · winter colour
plant.visual: Fiery red new growth and winter colour on a compact evergreen · fine, bamboo-like leaves · year-round structure
plant.water: Water regularly in the first season, then only in prolonged dry spells; pots need regular watering in summer.
